title: Coverings of semi-representable objects are stable under composition and base change
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ the category of semi-representable objects over $X$, with its coverings [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. (1) If $a:K\to L$ and $b:L\to M$ are coverings in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, then $b\circ a:K\to M$ is a covering. (2) If $a:K\to L$ is a covering and $c:L'\to L$ is any morphism of $\mathrm{SR}(X)$, then the fibre product $L'\times_LK$ in $\mathrm{SR}(X)$ exists, and its projection $L'\times_LK\to L'$ is a covering, where $L'\times_LK$ is the fibre product of [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits] (2) (applied to $\mathcal C=X_{\Et}$): for $K=\{K_i\}_{i\in I}$, $L=\{L_j\}_{j\in J}$, $L'=\{L'_l\}_{l\in J'}$, $a=(\alpha,a_i)$, $c=(\gamma,c_l)$, it is the family $\{L'_l\times_{c_l,L_{\gamma(l)},a_i}K_i\}_{(l,i)\in J'\times I,\ \gamma(l)=\alpha(i)}$, and the projection has index map $(l,i)\mapsto l$ and components the first projections.

proof.text: Write S(a,j) for the sieve in the definition of a semi-representable covering [def-weil-pbc-semi-representable-object]. For an etale object T and h:T\to L_j, membership h\in S(a,j) is equivalent to the existence of a morphism t:\{T\}\to K with t\gg a=\{j,h\} (here \gg denotes composition in Lean order, first the left map and then the right map). Indeed, membership in a generated sieve is exactly a factorization h=r\gg(a_i followed by the equality transport) for some i with a.f(i)=j; this defines t with index i and component r. Conversely, evaluate the equality t\gg a=\{j,h\} on the unique source index to obtain that index equality and the required factorization. The private Lean helper componentSieve_mem_iff proves this equivalence directly using Sieve.mem_ofArrows_iff and FormalCoproduct.hom_ext_iff.

For composition fix a target index n of M, and let R=S(a\gg b,n). The sieve S(b,n) is covering. Apply transitivity of the Grothendieck topology [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. If h:T\to M_n belongs to S(b,n), step 1 gives t:\{T\}\to L with t\gg b=\{n,h\}. Put i=t.f(*) and t_0=t.\varphi(*). The pullback of the covering sieve S(a,i) along t_0 covers T. This pullback is contained in R.pullback(h): for any k:Z\to T in it, step 1 gives s:\{Z\}\to K with s\gg a=\{i,k\gg t_0\}. The latter is the composite of the one-component morphism induced by k with t. Therefore s\gg(a\gg b)=\{n,k\gg h\}, so step 1 proves k\gg h\in R. Upward closure makes R.pullback(h) covering, and transitivity makes R covering. Lean uses GrothendieckTopology.transitive, pullback_stable and superset_covering, without any separate etale-covering composition theorem.

For base change let P=L\prime\times_L K with first projection p; its existence is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits]. Fix j\in L\prime.I. By the pullback axiom of the small etale topology [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], S(a,c.f(j)).pullback(c.\varphi(j)) covers L\prime_j. It is contained in S(p,j): if h:T\to L\prime_j belongs to the former, step 1 gives t:\{T\}\to K with t\gg a=\{c.f(j),h\gg c.\varphi(j)\}=\{j,h\}\gg c. The pullback universal property gives u= pullback.lift(\{j,h\},t):\{T\}\to P, and u\gg p=\{j,h\}. Step 1 gives h\in S(p,j). Upward closure (GrothendieckTopology.superset_covering) proves S(p,j) covering. This works for the chosen categorical pullback directly; no explicit reindexing or separate etale-covering base-change theorem is required.

Proof in four steps: notation (covering = componentwise covering family of X_et, composition law); (1) by the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition plus the reindexing bijection i -> (alpha(i), i) written out (Stacks calls it immediate); (2) fibre product from the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits (2) with X_et's fibre products from def-weil-pbc-etale-site, and the covering property componentwise from the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change. Statement made precise (not changed in content): (2) now says the fibre product exists and names it as the one of lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits (2), with its index set and projection, so the claim does not depend on a choice of fibre product; stmt_dep lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits added. Stacks proves (1),(2) for SR(C) and transfers to SR(C,X)=SR(C/X); here the site is X_et directly (objects already over X), which is the same thing. No new node; the existing Mathlib searches of the item (three kinds) stand.
